claims `plugin/**` and `skills/**` so that EVERY content change reaches the

`default` is NOT a general floor, and should not be read as one. verify-gate
falls back to it only when the matched rules contributed NO commands at all
(verify-gate.sh:247), so with rules this broad the only way to reach it is a
turn that changes nothing but files inside the two `run: []` rules - in
practice a graphify-out-only or workflow-only turn. It is kept because those
are real turns and 7s of smoke is a better answer there than nothing.
There is deliberately no `always` key: any entry in it would make `cmds`
non-empty every time and `default` unreachable.
`seconds` is the rule's MEASURED cost, and it is the field verify-gate
reads for the Stop budget (verify.stopBudgetSeconds, default 60). It
replaces nothing: `why` keeps the reason, `seconds` carries the number,
because the costs used to live only as prose inside `why` ("8s", "29s",
"245s") and nothing could parse them. A rule with NO `seconds` is UNKNOWN
cost, which is NOT free: it always runs and the gate says its cost is
unstated. Most rules here are deliberately in that state - only the ones
actually timed carry a number, and filling the rest in by guesswork would
be exactly the fiction the field exists to replace. Re-time rather than
trusting these: measured on a quiet tree 2026-09-18/19, and the whole-suite
185 is the midpoint of five runs spanning 157-201s, which is itself a
reason to treat it as approximate.

Round 1 found 2 BLOCK + 4 FIX: role-write-guard.ps1's python resolver started as the same un-hardened one-liner pm-pulse.ps1's and verify-gate.ps1's own headers name as a bug, so it was replaced with a third byte-identical copy of Resolve-CrewPython; role-write-guard.sh's own resolver started as the shared, unfiltered `_common.sh` crew_py() and gained its own WindowsApps-stub rejection so the two shell flavours of this one hook cannot enforce different decisions on the same machine; a repo config that EXISTS but fails to parse (or whose `guards` key is not an object) now forces `block` rather than silently resolving to `off` (`crew_config.repo_config_is_corrupt`); scope is judged against the REAL, symlink/junction-resolved path, not the lexical one, closing a `.crew/link -> src/` escape (tested with an actual Windows junction via `mklink /J` and a POSIX symlink, both created for real on this machine, not simulated); `_normalise_role` strips only a leading `crew:` prefix rather than the last `:`-segment of anything, so `other-plugin:analyst` no longer collides with crew's own `analyst` deny-list entry; a non-object JSON payload or a non-string `file_path` degrades to 'cannot classify' instead of an uncaught exception exiting 1, which `PreToolUse` treats as a non-blocking pass-through; and `.crew/guard.log` now carries the `reason` column (`no-agent-type` / `unknown-role:<value>`) the module docstring already promised but the row-building code never wrote. Round 2 (a probe on the round-1 fix) found one more: `pm` writing OUTSIDE the repo entirely (the harness-sanctioned scratchpad) was refused, when this guard's whole purpose is the REPO's write scope -- fixed with `role_write_guard._is_outside_repo_lexically`, checked on the LEXICAL path only, never the symlink-resolved one, so a symlink staged inside `.crew/` pointing at an in-repo but out-of-scope directory stays refused by the round-1 real-path check rather than being swept into the new exception; confirmed with `os.path.islink` after bash's own `ln -s` silently fell back to a plain directory on this machine and produced a false pass. test_role_write_guard.py grew from 35 to 70 cases across four probe rounds. Round 3 (crew_config.repo_config_is_corrupt's sibling in the same commit series) redefined the outside-repo exception from role_write_guard._is_outside_repo_lexically (judged on the LEXICAL path, wrongly still refusing a symlink staged inside the repo whose target escapes it entirely) to role_write_guard._is_outside_repo (judged on the REAL resolved path, matching the in-scope check it sits beside), flipping two must-block cases to must-allow and adding a PowerShell/junction twin of the still-refused in-repo-out-of-scope case. Round 4, a PowerShell-security-hardening specialist review of role-write-guard.ps1, found and fixed four more: a launch failure (the resolved interpreter cannot actually be started) left $LASTEXITCODE null and `exit $LASTEXITCODE` silently evaluated to 0, so a restricted role's write went through unjudged -- fixed with a try/catch plus a null-exit-code check that falls back to a small PowerShell-side classification (deny-list + pm) only for THIS one failure mode; stdin was read via [Console]::In.ReadToEnd(), which decodes with the OEM codepage and silently mangles non-ASCII characters and a leading UTF-8 BOM, unlike role-write-guard.sh's byte-transparent read -- fixed by reading raw bytes, stripping a BOM, and forcing UTF-8 on the way back out through the pipe; Resolve-CrewPython never executed a candidate to prove it was real (role-write-guard.sh's resolver does) and `Get-Command -All` walked past a WindowsApps stub to a SAME-NAMED real python further down PATH, while bash's `command -v` takes only the first match per name and moves to the NEXT name -- so role-write-guard.ps1 now executes each candidate and mirrors the .sh's name-order exactly, which means it is DELIBERATELY no longer byte-identical to verify-gate.ps1's and pm-pulse.ps1's copies (a new two-way parity test plus a divergence tripwire replaced the old three-way one); and a missing role_write_guard.py exited 2 with a bare CPython file-not-found error, indistinguishable from a real block -- fixed with an explicit existence check and a crew-specific diagnostic, still exiting 2. PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0: zero findings both before and after. These hooks can BLOCK a turn, so CLAUDE.md requires must-block and must-allow cases. This is a missing tool, not a failed check. Install PowerShell 7." >&2; exit 127'
rules.why: 3s. Every .ps1 here is Windows-only end to end, so a call to a cmdlet that does not exist parses cleanly and fails only on the one platform nothing here can run. PROVEN red by appending Invoke-TotallyMadeUpCmdlet to plugin/crew/hooks/scripts/guard.ps1 - a file REMOVED in 0.19.52, so that exact proof can no longer be re-run. The measurement stands as a record of what was done; re-prove it against any registered .ps1 (promote-gate.ps1, verify-gate.ps1) rather than trusting this line, and do not rewrite the file named above, which would falsify what was actually measured. The interpreter is RESOLVED, not named. This file is TRACKED as of 2026-09-14, so it travels to clones that are not this machine, and a hardcoded /c/Program Files/PowerShell/7/pwsh fails on every one of them - verify-gate.sh runs this command and blocks completion on a non-zero exit, so even a Linux clone with pwsh ON PATH was blocked by this rule. Order matters: bare `pwsh` first, then `pwsh.exe` and the Windows locations with AND without the .exe suffix - under WSL the reachable binary is the Windows one and is named pwsh.exe, so omitting the suffix reported TOOL MISSING on a box where PowerShell was installed and usable, because CLAUDE.md records that a bare `pwsh` is not always on Git Bash's PATH. When nothing resolves it exits 127 with TOOL MISSING on stderr rather than 0 - a tool that could not run must never report as a check that passed. NOTE the script's two known limitations (README of _verify): CI mode enumerates via `git ls-files`, so an UNTRACKED .ps1 is invisible to it, and `param([string]$Path)` takes one path, silently dropping the rest of a list.
